items.title: Clayton Duerr Interview, 1972-04-17
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...you see Paul Barberin and Louis Russell... And I'm sure you knew them all around New York at one time or another... [INTERVIEWEE] Yeah, I knew Pop.

ctx.x: Well yeah, that's how I come to... Yeah, well you... But I didn't know you had to win. You were from somewhere down here but I didn't know where.

Yeah, well all those guys, you see Paul Barberin and Louis Russell and Pop Foster and Red Allen and Albert Nicholas and all those guys were with Louis Russell and Louis Armstrong, you know, and the band, the same band. And I'm sure you knew them all around New York at one time or another, you knew Pop.

Yeah, I knew Pop. I knew Fats Duarte was pretty good. We used to go up to the hall and after hours and time, you know, I'll tell you about that place called the Clam House. They had a big colored piano playing piano and all the piano players used to come up and sit and play. Like Willie the Lion used to come in and sometime I would come in. Not too much of them coming on the floor. But they had a different kind of play that she didn't play, I mean you know, Phil will play. That's wrong. Oh God. Moke was up there…
